answer: Latency-Challenge Spawn Ledger: each new agent identity must answer a random challenge whose delay rises with the count of identities sharing its network path, so clones queue behind siblings. A falcon-class verifier samples path timing continuously. Under load, a dune-like backlog accumulates and each duplicate's compute cost grows superlinearly, while a zephyr-fast honest agent on a fresh path passes cheaply. Cloning past a few identities costs more than operating one, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
